land.text: Corsica, 'the whole island except for a few coastal towns' which Paoli's forces drove the Genoese from

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Predecessor: Republic of Genoa'. The page does not name the coastal towns Genoa kept.

successors.note: Infobox 'Successor: Kingdom of France'; Genoa had sold its claim in the Treaty of Versailles (15 May 1768).

capitals.name: Corte
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Corte'; 'He founded a university at Corte'. Corte is not in the gazetteer.

rulers.name: Pasquale Paoli
rulers.note: Infobox 'Leader 1755-1769'; he took refuge in Great Britain after Ponte Novu. The page gives no title.

correction.text: Corsica without the few coastal towns Genoa kept: 'drove the Genoese from the whole island except for a few coastal towns'; independence 'proclaimed in July 1755'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Corsican shape starts in 1757 but the infobox gives 'Independence declared: July 1755'. The page does not say when the Genoese were driven back, so the 1757 shape is bridged back (confidence 1 for the extent). The page names none of the towns Genoa kept.

11,217 km2 for 1757-1762: the whole island drawn as one block (34 cells; the island is 8,680 km2, the rest is cell overshoot). The page gives no infobox area; it says Genoa kept 'a few coastal towns' without naming them, so the shape slightly overstates the republic's hold on the coast. The governing form changed in 1762 ('Modified parliamentary constitutional republic under an anocracy (from 1762)') with no border change.

11,217 km2 for 1763-1768, the same outline. Capraia, taken from Genoa in 1767 and to be returned to Genoa under the Treaty of Versailles (15 May 1768), is too small for a land cell and is in the ledger only. Cliopatria's end in 1768 is the year Genoa sold its claim and France began the conquest; the republic fell in May 1769.

correction.text: the same outline until the conquest: 'Conquered: 9 May 1769', after the Battle of Ponte Novu 'in May 1769'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends the row in 1768 but the republic held its interior until the French victory at Ponte Novu in May 1769 ('France gained full military control of the island following the Battle of Ponte Novu in 1769', Treaty of Versailles page). The ledger removes the island on 9 May 1769.

ledger.note: July 1755: Corsica proclaims its independence under Pasquale Paoli. 'It was proclaimed in July 1755 by Pasquale Paoli, who was seeking independence from the Republic of Genoa'; he 'drove the Genoese from the whole island except for a few coastal towns'. The page does not date the expulsion or name the towns.

region.text: Corsica, the whole island except for a few coastal towns

ledger.note: 1767: the Corsicans take Capraia. 'In 1767, Corsica took the island of Capraia from the Genoese.' Capraia is too small for a gazetteer land cell (a 12 km disc stands for it).

15 May 1768: the Treaty of Versailles has Capraia returned to Genoa. 'the treaty also established that France would return to Genoa the possession of neighboring Capraia island'. The page does not date the handover; the treaty date is used.

September 1768: France begins the conquest of Corsica. 'In September 1768, France began its conquest of Corsica' after 'Genoa sold Corsica to France' in the Treaty of Versailles of 15 May 1768 (infobox: 'Genoa de jure cedes Corsica to France'); the Corsican Republic page dates the Battle of Borgo to 8-9 October 1768.

region.text: Corsica, the island France set out to conquer

ledger.note: 9 May 1769: the republic is beaten at Ponte Novu. 'in May 1769, at the Battle of Ponte Novu they were defeated by vastly superior forces commanded by the Comte de Vaux'; infobox 'Conquered: 9 May 1769'.
9 May 1769: France conquers Corsica. Infobox 'Conquered: 9 May 1769', 'Successor: Kingdom of France'; Paoli was 'obliged to take refuge in the Kingdom of Great Britain'.
May 1769: the Corsican Republic ends; the island passes to the Kingdom of France.

wars.name: Corsican struggle for independence from Genoa

zones.text: the whole island except for a few coastal towns

wars.outcome: The Genoese were driven from the whole island except a few coastal towns; the Corsicans took Capraia in 1767; in the Treaty of Versailles of 15 May 1768 Genoa sold its claim to France.
wars.note: The page gives the independence (July 1755), the 1764 request for French troops (Treaty of Versailles page) and the 1768 sale; it does not name a war or a campaign before 1768.

wars.name: French conquest of Corsica
wars.outcome: France began the conquest in September 1768 (Borgo, 8-9 October 1768) and gained full military control after Ponte Novu in May 1769 ('Conquered: 9 May 1769'); Paoli fled to Great Britain.
wars.note: Genoa is a belligerent only as the seller of its claim.

certainty.note: The republic held the interior and Genoa kept a few unnamed coastal towns, so the coastline is the island's outline but the frontier between Corsican and Genoese land is approximate throughout.

sources.title: Corsican Republic
sources.note: Main source: independence July 1755, capital Corte, Paoli, Capraia 1767, Borgo and Ponte Novu, conquest 9 May 1769. No area given; silent on named towns.

sources.title: Treaty of Versailles (1768)
sources.note: 15 May 1768: Genoa sells Corsica to France; Capraia returned to Genoa; France begins the conquest in September 1768.

notes:
Cliopatria's Corsican Republic row (1757-1768, two identical 11,217 km2 shapes) is shifted against the page: independence was proclaimed in July 1755 and the republic was conquered on 9 May 1769, so two new keyframes (1755-1756, 1769) bridge the shape at both ends. The pages do not date the Genoese retreat, so the 1755 extent is confidence 1.
Unresolved: which coastal towns Genoa kept (not named on either page); whether Capraia was actually handed back in 1768 (the Treaty of Versailles page says France 'would return' it); the kingdom of Corsica of 1736 and the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom of 1794-1796 are not covered by Cliopatria's row and are not in this dossier. Gazetteer names needed: Corte (place), Capraia (a small island: no land cell, so the ledger regions of 1767 and 1768 resolve to no cells and are warnings).
